_: T2.0 NAVCUT SPIKE (workflows/plans/navmesh.md) — a FALSIFICATION experiment, not a feature demo. Question: does an L_NAVCUT collision volume authored by ModForge (base CollisionMarker 0x000021 + CollisionLayer 49 + XPRM box) actually switch vanilla navmesh off at runtime, so an NPC paths AROUND it? Design = a matched A/B pair 800 units apart on the Whiterun main street (WhiterunWorld = Skyrim.esm:0x01A26F). BOTH lanes are byte-for-byte identical — same NPC, same package, same two markers 310 units apart, same 4 sign posts marking the barrier line — EXCEPT lane A has a navCut box across the middle and lane B does not. READ-OUT: if the TEST NPC's path differs from the CONTROL's in ANY way (arcs around the post line, refuses to cross, hugs the posts' ends) the navcut works; if both walk the same straight line through their posts, L_NAVCUT is dead for us and route A of the plan is falsified. Every coordinate below was picked by reading Skyrim.esm's own navmesh — all 14 are verified to sit on a live triangle, and the floor z is the interpolated triangle height at that point (an XMarkerHeading does NOT snap to the floor, so a guessed z silently kills the patrol).

navmesh._: autoNavCuts OFF on purpose: the spike must have exactly ONE navcut in it — the one authored below. Anything auto-generated would muddy a falsification test.

packages._: Patrol template (Skyrim.esm:0x017723). Route = the linkedRefs loop A1 -> A2 -> A1. The straight line between the two markers runs dead through the navCut box.
Identical package for the CONTROL lane — same template, same radius, same loop shape. The ONLY difference between the lanes is the navCut box.

navCuts._: THE EXPERIMENT. A 520 x 140 x 220 box lying ACROSS lane A's patrol line, padded outward by 32 (half an actor's width — the engine tests actors as ZERO-VOLUME points, so an unpadded box leaks). Emitted XPRM Bounds = 584 x 204 x 284, centred at (21750, -7625, -3510.6): X 21458..22042, Y -7727..-7523, Z -3652..-3368. The floor under it runs -3583..-3548, so the box straddles the navmesh plane by a wide margin. It covers 7 vanilla triangle centroids and intersects 12 triangles. The 204-unit-thick forbidden band is far wider than an NPC's step, so no path can hop it — the NPC must round one of the X ends (21458 / 22042), both of which have open navmesh.

placements._: TEST NPC, spawned on marker A1 (floor z read off the vanilla navmesh triangle under it).
Lane A north marker. 53 units clear of the padded box's north edge — enough ground to stand on and start a path from.
Lane A south marker, 310 units due south of A1. The direct line crosses the box.
CONTROL NPC, spawned on marker B1. Identical build to the tester.

The 8 sign posts (SignWRPost01, 18x18x192) are the only thing you can SEE — a navcut volume is invisible. Four of them bracket lane A's box; four sit at the SAME offsets in lane B, where there is no box. They are 18x18, far under navmesh.minFootprint, so they neither cut navmesh nor meaningfully block anyone — an NPC walks straight between them. If the TEST NPC refuses to cross ITS post line while the CONTROL strolls through its identical one, the only possible cause is the box.
